subject: Image 1 is a painted riverside reference. Produce NEW, reusable ORIGINAL ground material samples for that same restrained 2D pixel game, NOT a landscape. A borderless rectangular MATERIAL ATLAS, two bands each covering exactly HALF the canvas, edge to edge. TOP HALF: flat olive/muted mossy GREEN grass bank, about ninety percent continuous quiet medium olive fill. In a few places little connected 2–4 square-pixel low grass tufts, little flattened herb and short darker moss marks, with some empty space larger than the marks. No steep steps, rocks or sprouting trees on this grass. BOTTOM HALF: muted dark warm grey/brown damp cut earth with small rounded / chipped embedded SLATE pebbles; these are a horizontal BANK MATERIAL field of broken overlapping earthy/clayey patches, no perspective scene or background, a few muted grey stone tops only a few logical pixels across; no large boulders, cobblestones, outlines around every cell or geometric brickwork. The dividing line is a plain straight halfway cut for packing, no label, frame or inset. Fill the whole image. Work first as a native coarse 120×80 logical pixel tile source blown up with nearest neighbour, not as a smooth large painting. Hard step edges and chunky flat ink clusters with/selective minute highlights, 4–5 closely related muted ink values per material. Use the reference for MATERIAL LANGUAGE and pixel density, but base colours should be readable in neutral shadowless light; the game will add its own localized moonlight, lamps, shore glow and mirrored objects. No river, trees, sky, person, lamp, stone marker, baked directional shadows, bloom, shadows, text, icons, dither grain or photoreal textures.
